A.explanation: If one resistor were $15 \Omega$ the other would be $19 \Omega$, giving a parallel resistance of about $8.4 \Omega$, not $7.4 \Omega$.

B.explanation: If both were $17 \Omega$ the series total would be $34 \Omega$ but the parallel total would be $8.5 \Omega$, which is larger than $7.4 \Omega$.

C.explanation: With $23 \Omega$ and $11 \Omega$ the series sum is $34 \Omega$ and the parallel value is $(23 \times 11)/34 \approx 7.4 \Omega$.

D.explanation: If one resistor were $27 \Omega$ the other would be $7 \Omega$, giving a parallel resistance of about $5.6 \Omega$, not $7.4 \Omega$.

hints: Notice the two given totals: $R_1 + R_2 = 34 \Omega$ for series and $R_1 R_2/(R_1+R_2) = 7.4 \Omega$ for parallel.
Combine the two series-parallel rules to find the product $R_1 R_2$ by multiplying the $7.4 \Omega$ parallel value by the $34 \Omega$ series sum.
Let one resistance be $R$, so the other is $34 - R$, then solve $R(34-R) = 251.6$ and check which listed value fits.
walkthrough: Call the resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$. For series, $R_1 + R_2 = 34 \Omega$.
For parallel, $1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$, which rearranges to $R_p = R_1 R_2/(R_1+R_2) = 7.4 \Omega$.
Substitute the series sum: $R_1 R_2/34 = 7.4$, so $R_1 R_2 = 7.4 \times 34 = 251.6 \, \Omega^2$.
Solving gives $R = [34 + \sqrt{34^2 - 4 \times 251.6}]/2 \approx 23.1 \Omega$, with the other resistor about $10.9 \Omega$.
The value $23 \Omega$ matches one of the listed options. This is option C.
